item.title: PM defends UN trip
item.description: PRESIDENT Ratu Naiqama Lalabalavu is entitled to take a nine-member delegation to the United Nations General Assembly (UNGA) in New York next month. Prime Minister Sitiveni Rabuka said this as he defended the need for the President to travel with a range of official and support staff.
item.content:encoded:
PRESIDENT Ratu Naiqama Lalabalavu is entitled to take a nine-member delegation to the United Nations General Assembly (UNGA) in New York next month.

Prime Minister Sitiveni Rabuka said this as he defended the need for the President to travel with a range of official and support staff.

The President has been asked to lead Fiji’s delegation to the 81st UNGA, following a formal request from Mr Rabuka to permanent secretary for Foreign Affairs, Raijeli Taga.

Mr Rabuka said the decision was intended to give the President an opportunity to deliver Fiji’s national address to the General Assembly during his first term in office.

“The previous president, Ratu Wiliame Katonivere, and in the four-year term of my government I’ve done it twice, and each of my presidents have done it once,” he said.

“Our new president will do it this time.”

Documents attached to the letter show a quoted $F45,668 business and first-class fare, while a separate itinerary for his aide-de-camp lists an economy-class fare of $F5778.

The figure does not include accommodation, visas, ground transportation, meals or other expenses associated with the delegation.

Questions have also been raised over the inclusion of the President’s personal butler, physician, and a domestic staff in the nine-member entourage.

“There is nothing special about the size, it’s about the normal size,” the PM said.

“My delegation was around seven people when I went.”

The Prime Minister said the President’s position as Head of State meant he was entitled to make decisions appropriate to his office.

item.title: Clearance system to modernise
item.description: FIJI’S police clearance service, which generated $4.3 million in revenue last year, is set for a major digital overhaul aimed at making applications faster and more accessible. Minister for Policing Ioane Naivalurua told Parliament recently that the Fiji Police Force processed 52,694 police clearance applications last year — an increase of 8482 from 2024.
item.content:encoded:
FIJI’S police clearance service, which generated $4.3 million in revenue last year, is set for a major digital overhaul aimed at making applications faster and more accessible.

Minister for Policing Ioane Naivalurua told Parliament recently that the Fiji Police Force processed 52,694 police clearance applications last year — an increase of 8482 from 2024.

“A Police Clearance Certificate is an official document confirming whether an applicant has any criminal record in Fiji,” he said.

Mr Naivalurua said the service was among the police force’s most in-demand services and was required for employment, visas, residency and overseas study.

He said the Government was working with development partners to move the largely manual process online.

The new system will allow applicants to submit applications online, make secure digital payments and access the service without having to travel.

Mr Naivalurua said it would also improve identification verification, processing and tracking while strengthening privacy and security safeguards.

He said the initiative was being developed with support from the United Nations Capital Development Fund, Pacific Digital Economy Programme and Web Media South Pacific.

“The new system, when this comes into force, will be intended to modernise what has traditionally been a largely manual process.”

Mr Naivalurua said the police force was also working with the Ministry of Justice, Vodafone and Bank of South Pacific on the digital payment integration system.

item.title: Rabuka calls for courage to drive national development forward
item.description: THE Prime Minister Sitiveni Rabuka has warned that a lingering cloud of fear is holding Fijians back from realising their true economic and social potential. Speaking at the 25th anniversary celebrations of FRIEND Fiji in Lautoka yesterday, Mr Rabuka recounted a recent address to the Fiji Indigenous Business Council where he confronted an auditorium gripped by silence.
item.content:encoded:
THE Prime Minister Sitiveni Rabuka has warned that a lingering cloud of fear is holding Fijians back from realising their true economic and social potential.

Speaking at the 25th anniversary celebrations of FRIEND Fiji in Lautoka yesterday, Mr Rabuka recounted a recent address to the Fiji Indigenous Business Council where he confronted an auditorium gripped by silence.

“If you live in fear, you’ll never get out of the shell,”he said.

“You’ll never get out of the house. You’ll never get out of your limitations.

Mr Rabuka emphasized that poverty could not be understood through income alone, pointing to broader systemic pressure including the rising cost of living, climate-related shocks, food security, and limited access to economic infrastructure.

“In 2019 the household income and expenditure survey provided a very important baseline reporting that approximately 29.9 per cent of Fijians were living below the basic needs poverty line. We have to recognise other aspects in which poverty may be defined and measured across the nation and also ways in which we can get out of those limitations — do not allow ourselves to be shackled by the notion that we are poor.”

Mr Rabuka said the Government had committed in the 2026-2027 budget to assisting roughly 130,000 citizens through existing social welfare and pension initiatives.

“Achieving higher and more inclusive growth means creating opportunities beyond our major urban centres.

“Rural and maritime communities must be connected to markets, infrastructure, finance, technology, and skills so that they can participate meaningfully in the national economy.”

item.title: HIV care – the power of open dialogue
item.description: HEALTH professionals should not completely dismiss patients who express an interest in using traditional or herbal medicine alongside standard treatments for HIV, says HIV clinician Dr Dashika Balak. Speaking at the 2026 Pacific HIV Symposium at the Sheraton Fiji Golf Resort and Spa in Nadi recently, Dr Balak emphasised the importance of maintaining an open, supportive dialogue with individuals se
item.content:encoded:
HEALTH professionals should not completely dismiss patients who express an interest in using traditional or herbal medicine alongside standard treatments for HIV, says HIV clinician Dr Dashika Balak.

Speaking at the 2026 Pacific HIV Symposium at the Sheraton Fiji Golf Resort and Spa in Nadi recently, Dr Balak emphasised the importance of maintaining an open, supportive dialogue with individuals seeking alternative options.

Dr Balak said a heavy-handed or dismissive approach from medical practitioners often led patients to disengage entirely from necessary medical care.

“We do have a lot of patients who come in and prefer to go on herbal or traditional medication and what we do is we do create a safe space for them where we do talk about this,” she said.

“We discuss why they want to go on herbal medication, what is their perception of herbal medication, how antiretroviral therapy is going to help them, what is the evidence behind the medications.”

Rather than shutting down the conversation, medical professionals should guide patients toward an approach where conventional, life-saving antiretroviral therapy remains a central pillar of their health routine.

“At the end of the day, we never discourage them or say no from taking because the moment you say no, that is when they switch off.

“My advice to my patients is, if you want to take your herbal medicine, if you want to take your traditional medication, I don’t stop you but how I want you to work with me is you take my medication as well, you can take your medication at night, you take my medication in the morning and it works.”

Dr Balak stressed that fostering trust between the clinician and the patient remained critical to achieving positive long-term health outcomes.

“The point is, the moment you say no, that’s it, you lose your patient.”

item.title: FRIEND boosts rural growth
item.description: THE Foundation for Rural Integrated Enterprises and Development or FRIEND has officially been commended by the Fijian Government for a quarter-century of transforming local skills, traditional knowledge, and community resources into thriving, sustainable livelihoods. Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Industries, Commerce, Business Development and Public Enterprises Manoa Kamikamica lauded the
item.content:encoded:
THE Foundation for Rural Integrated Enterprises and Development or FRIEND has officially been commended by the Fijian Government for a quarter-century of transforming local skills, traditional knowledge, and community resources into thriving, sustainable livelihoods.

Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Industries, Commerce, Business Development and Public Enterprises Manoa Kamikamica lauded the milestone during celebrations marking a decade of collaboration between FRIEND and the Motibhai Group of Companies.

Mr Kamikamica emphasised that behind every successful commercial venture lay a household touched by opportunity.

“Behind every carton of product that leaves this building for a supermarket shelf, there is a family,” he said.

Founded in 2001 by the now Minister for Women, Children and Social Protection, Sashi Kiran, FRIEND has expanded its reach across more than 500 communities.

The organisation has empowered over 6000 women and supported hundreds of farmers through initiatives like the EU-backed GROW program, advancing organic farming, beekeeping, and food preservation.

Through its decade-long alliance with Motibhai, 31 distinct, fully Fijian-made FRIEND Fiji Style products now occupy prominent retail shelves nationwide.

This success aligns seamlessly with the national economic vision. With micro, small, and medium enterprises currently contributing approximately 18 per cent of Fiji’s Gross Domestic Product, the Government aims to elevate that figure to 40 per cent under the MSME Strategic Plan spanning 2025 to 2030.

Backed by millions in targeted grant allocations and extensive training programs, the ministry continues to build an ecosystem where local entrepreneurs can thrive.

Mr Kamikamica said that FRIEND’s enduring journey served as a vital blueprint for national development, proving that small enterprises flourish when deep-rooted community skills connected directly with commercial opportunity.

item.title: Elderly care homes open in Koroipita
item.description: TWO aged-care facilities have opened in Koroipita, Lautoka, providing full-time care for elderly residents and people with special needs. Koroipita Model Towns Charitable Trust general manager Paul Forrest said the initiative reflected the growing need for aged-care services within the community.
item.content:encoded:
TWO aged-care facilities have opened in Koroipita, Lautoka, providing full-time care for elderly residents and people with special needs.

Koroipita Model Towns Charitable Trust general manager Paul Forrest said the initiative reflected the growing need for aged-care services within the community.

“Providing homes is only the beginning; we must also respond to the changing health, care and social needs of the people who live here,” he said.

“Social housing also comes with social needs.”

Mr Forrest said 62 residents were in their 60s, while 27 were aged 70 oand above, with the oldest resident aged 76.

He said 15 residents, including adults and children with special needs, required home assistance ranging from one hour a day to full-time care.

“These numbers highlight the growing need for aged-care services in our community, especially as there are limited options elsewhere.”

Mr Forrest said plans were also underway to develop an outdoor area where residents could enjoy fresh air and social interaction.

Minister for Women Sashi Kiran said the facilities represented the first model of community care at Koroipita.

She commended Mr Forrest for his vision and thanked the board and trustees for supporting the initiative.

“I’m really grateful for Paul’s vision – for opening yourself to the challenge, and I thank the board and trustees for opening to this idea of building aged-care facilities within the community,” Ms Kiran said.

Meanwhile, Latter-day Saints Charities donated household items for residents with support from the Ministry of Women, Children and Social Protection.

item.title: Authority raises alarm on home fires
item.description: A DEVASTATING afternoon fire on Friday reduced a Drasa Dam Rd home in Lautoka to ashes, leaving five people homeless and sparking fresh concerns from authorities over a surge in structural blazes across the Western Division. Ravindra Gopal Naidu was at work when his nine-year-old son called with the terrifying news. His mother, grandfather, and son were inside when flames erupted in a corner room,
item.content:encoded:
A DEVASTATING afternoon fire on Friday reduced a Drasa Dam Rd home in Lautoka to ashes, leaving five people homeless and sparking fresh concerns from authorities over a surge in structural blazes across the Western Division.

Ravindra Gopal Naidu was at work when his nine-year-old son called with the terrifying news. His mother, grandfather, and son were inside when flames erupted in a corner room, but all escaped safely.

“Everything was destroyed, we could not save anything, but now I want to build my house,” he said.

“We are staying temporarily at my sister’s place in Nadi, but I am grateful no one was injured.”

National Fire Authority chief executive officer Puamau Sowane confirmed the Lautoka fire station received the emergency call at 2pm. Two fire engines and an ambulance arrived at the scene within 23 minutes, finding the structure fully engulfed.

Firefighters utilised stored water tanks to extinguish the blaze, preventing further spread.

Total damage to the 19-by-10-metre property is estimated at $60,000.

Investigators are sifting through the ruins to determine the cause.

Mr Sowane raised his concerns over the region’s trajectory, noting that August alone has recorded more than eight structural fires in the Western Division.

“The only one that can avoid fires is us, the owners of our homes,” he said.

Mr Sowane urged parents and homeowners to remain vigilant with electrical appliances, cooking, and fire safety during the school holidays.

item.title: Couple arrested with suspected drugs, housebreaking tools
item.description: A 41-year-old man and his 35-year-old wife are in Police custody after they were allegedly found in possession of white powder believed to be illicit drugs and housebreaking implements. The couple was arrested at around 1am yesterday after Police stopped and searched their vehicle at a checkpoint in Dokanaisuva.
item.content:encoded:
A 41-year-old man and his 35-year-old wife are in Police custody after they were allegedly found in possession of white powder believed to be illicit drugs and housebreaking implements.

The couple was arrested at around 1am yesterday after Police stopped and searched their vehicle at a checkpoint in Dokanaisuva.

Police say the vehicle was also found to have an expired wheel tax, while the man, who was driving, did not have a valid driving licence.

The couple remains in custody as Police investigations continue.

Police are expected to establish the nature of the suspected drugs and determine the circumstances surrounding the possession of the housebreaking implements.
